synopsis: High-volume model-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop testing targets thousands of runs per night on cloud or on-premises compute, with logic tests suited to commodity servers or containers and sensor tests assigned to GPU workers [f7138, f16220]. The illustrative budget buys ten single-GPU cloud instances running continuously for 122 days: about USD 54,490 for at most roughly 29,000 GPU-hours, limiting full-sensor-fidelity coverage and motivating tiered testing [f8869, f13548]. Cost per simulated hour depends on the measured real-time factor, so the example is not a quantified workload budget; the required compute remains unquantified and should be budgeted before mid-2027 [f13549, f14511]. Although compute is described as comparatively cheap relative to specialist labor, the skeptic's review flags compute and defect triage as potential bottlenecks, and recommends benchmarking preparation, correlation and triage before scaling infrastructure [f13550, f10789, f16235]. Parallel-execution licensing and intellectual-property rights also require explicit procurement attention: vendor cloud terms were not reviewed, export control and data residency were not researched, and technical access does not necessarily authorize cloud use [f8901, f8907, f8912, f8913, f10813].
